short: Profits kept in the business rather than paid out.
seoTitle: Retained Earnings — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Retained earnings are the accumulated profits a business has kept rather than distributed to its owners. Profits kept in the business rather than paid out.
definition: Retained earnings are the accumulated profits a business has kept rather than distributed to its owners. They appear under equity on the balance sheet and grow with each profitable year.
bodyHtml:
Why Retained Earnings matters

Retained earnings are the cheapest growth capital there is — no interest, no dilution. They are also the clearest measure of whether a business has genuinely built value over time.

Retained Earnings formula

Closing retained earnings = Opening + Net profit − Dividends or drawings

Accumulated losses reduce the balance and can turn it negative.

How Retained Earnings works in practice

They rise by profit and fall by losses and distributions. A business with years of profit and no retained earnings has been paying everything out, which limits its ability to fund its own growth.

faq.question: Are retained earnings cash?
faq.answer: No. They may be sitting in stock, equipment or receivables rather than in the bank.

faq.question: Can retained earnings be negative?
faq.answer: Yes. Accumulated losses exceeding past profits produce a negative balance.
